Subject: Partnership inquiry — ISV bundling & weights distribution

Hi Camila,

Hope you're well — I'm Ellen (Head of Partnerships at MosaicHub). We publish open-architecture models and are exploring ISV bundling partnerships so enterprise software vendors can include optimized inference artifacts with their products.

Key asks:
- Can Redwood host distro artifacts (weights, quantized variants) and gate access for ISVs without exposing raw weights to end customers?
- What controls & licensing language would you expect from the publisher side to allow redistribution as part of an ISV bundle (and where does attribution + liability typically live)?

Subject: Re: Partnership inquiry — ISV bundling & weights distribution

Hi Ellen — thanks for reaching out and for the sample. This is exactly the kind of model-publisher + ISV scenario we see a lot. High-level responses inline: 

- Host & gating: yes — Redwood can host model artifacts in a private bucket and expose inference through our Hosted API or via customer-specific Dedicated pools. We do not have to expose raw full-precision weights to the ISV’s end customers; instead we support serving sealed artifacts and offering inference endpoints (or signed binaries for on-prem bundles under Private deployments).

- Redistribution + licensing: we typically require a term sheet that covers permitted redistribution (bundled inference vs full weights), attribution, and permitted use cases. For enterprise redistribution we see three common lanes:
  1) "Endpoint-only" distribution — ISV bundles client that calls Redwood endpoints; publisher retains weights and liability management is simpler.
  2) "Encapsulated artifact" — publisher provides quantized/obfuscated artifacts with strict license that allows bundling but forbids re-distribution outside the ISV product.
  3) "Full redistribute" — rare for open-publisher commercial lanes; requires escrow and additional indemnities.

Next steps: can your legal team share a short term-sheet (you included one — thanks) and a list of required controls (audit logging, KMS, PSP/crypto requirements)? Also suggest a 30-min sync Thursday to align on a playbook approach (packaging, signatures, runtime compatibility).

Couple of internal folks copied to help scope (Grace: security/compliance; Sergio: partnerships ops).

Best,
Camila Reyes
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com

Thanks Camila — appreciate the clear lanes. Attaching a slightly expanded term sheet that clarifies permitted redistribution and required audit logs. Tech notes: we can provide quantized variants (int8) and a signature file for each artifact; we prefer your Hosted API + sealed artifact lane if possible.

Quick answers to your asks:
- Controls: KMS-backed keys for artifact signing; per-partner service accounts; per-route token scoping; audit log retention 12 months minimum; support for Private deployments (air-gapped) is good to have but not required for initial pilots.
- Liability: MosaicHub asks for limited indemnity when the model is used according to the permitted uses doc; we cannot indemnify downstream re-distributors.

Camila — short answers:
- Signed artifacts: yes, we can sign artifacts with a customer-specific KMS key and provide signature verification in our serving runtime. We can also store a copy in a private bucket and restrict access.
- Audit logs: we persist token-level logs; 12-month retention is within our enterprise offering (requires an advanced observability add-on).
- Compliance/escrow: if MosaicHub asks for escrow of full precision weights for "full redistribute" lane, that's a separate legal/ops project.

Sergio — from ops perspective, encapsulated endpoints are straightforward: create a model variant, apply a quantization profile, and push to a Dedicated pool. Typical lead time for a pilot (packaging + validation) is 2–3 weeks; billing aligns to tokens served and reserved capacity if they choose Dedicated.

I'll join the call on Thu.

Grace O'Connor
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Subject: MosaicHub / Redwood — proposed ISV distribution playbook & next steps

Hi Ellen — great sync yesterday. Per our discussion, here's a compact playbook and next steps so we have alignment: 

Playbook (summary):
1) Pilot lane: "Encapsulated artifact" — MosaicHub provides quantized/artifact + signature; Redwood hosts artifact in private bucket and exposes sealed endpoints to partner ISVs. No raw full-precision weights are distributed.
2) Controls: KMS-based signing, per-partner service accounts, per-route token scoping, 12-month audit logs (observability add-on), and rate limiting by partner.
3) Licensing: MosaicHub term-sheet + a Redwood partner addendum that clarifies indemnity and prohibits downstream redistribution outside the bundled product.
4) Ops timeline: packaging & quantization validation (1 week), staging validation (1 week), pilot launch on Dedicated pool (reserve for 1 month).

Action items:
- MosaicHub: confirm the final term-sheet and mark required controls in the Drive doc (link below).
- Redwood (Camila): produce a short partner playbook doc and DocuSign partner addendum draft.
- Redwood (Sergio): provide a proposed billing estimate for a 1-month Dedicated pilot (tokens + reserved capacity + observability add-on).

Doc links & sign: https://drive.google.com/mosaichub/specs-playbook | DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/Signing/MosaicHub-Partner-Playbook

If that looks good I'll route a DocuSign to MosaicHub Legal with the partner addendum to be reviewed this week.
